items.note: Story 1: Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery 1891.
Story 1: pay by pounds of butterfat by the test at the station where he delivered, not by weight.
Story 1: 'Under payment by weight, the glass would have cost nobody anything.'
Only Wilbur Teague (bookkeeper) appears; Effie Loomis and Hobart Sill are absent. One of three officers does not carry the item.
Son of Gideon stated, but manager 'from 1911' (Story 4, Story 6). The bolded year 1913 is wrong.
Story 6: the yearly 'station gain ... five and a quarter per cent, as usual, carried to the general account' line.
Story 1: Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896 on glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
List-type item, core fact present: weighed in, sampled, fixed 17.6 c.c. charge into a bottle whose neck is ruled for it, cream to Larrow Green, skim returned.
Story 2: Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice of 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Story 2 gives the full invoice: 6 doz pipettes marked 17.6 c.c. ... $77.93.
Story 4: 0.19 points, 'the same in every month, flush and winter alike'.
Nothing in Section A says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette or that the county had no burette.
Story 1: Keddie (1861-1934), 29 seasons 1896-1924; Story 7: dismissed 30 April 1925.
The test book is kept by Ansel from 1896 and he recorded every figure (Stories 1 and 5). Only 'test book' is bolded.
Section A never gives the 1896 season average of 3.80 against 3.61 from 1898. Both figures are required.
8 May-10 July, nine weeks and the question mark are all present, but the run says tests were 'markedly higher', unquantified. The bolded 3.80 is missing.
Story 3: married Orra, sister of Emmet Brant, the largest patron and biggest loser.
1919 circular present, but not Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why.
Story 7: died February 1934, charge never withdrawn; test book impounded 1925, to Historical Rooms 1959 (Story 8).
Story 3: six farms, Emmet's the largest.
Story 3: weigh book from 1 January 1897 (accepted); 'Scale weights always agreed'.
First complaint 1902. The run keeps the gaps apart (3.61 vs 3.78; 0.19 measured against the true 3.80, explicitly not against Larrow Green in E).
Jan-Mar 1908 is given and hay is reported as the committee's view, but the committee is not placed under Nyle Grigg, only 'came up in Grigg's sleigh'. Bolded element not met.
Story 3: 200,000 lb at 3.42; proportional error stated in Story 2 ('reads low by exactly the same proportion') and applied (3.42/0.95).
Story 3: to Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, to Hazel 1962.
Cudd's cheese factory at Alder Corners 'over the ridge'. Redlow Ridge is not named and Vessey County is not given as the factory's location (the ridge and county gate).
Four farms in the summer flush is present, but the bolded 'from 1915' is missing.
No independence statement; at most one element (the artifact). Two are required.
Only 'tested normally there'. No 0.19-higher figure and no overlapping seasons.
Story 4: 'The same milk tested normally there, so it was never the cows.'
Rosalie is Jerome's daughter and copied the figures for Ivy, but the bolded 'sixteen seasons' is absent.
Strawn is named and unrelated to anyone, but his circuit is dated from 1908 ('every visit from 1908 on'), not 1907.
Story 4: lactometer at every visit, never found added water.
Story 7: 12 June 1923, calibrated burette, condemned the whole lot.
Only 'drew no inference about the years before'. Nothing that he wrote no figure for the deficiency.
Replacement dates are right, but 'From 1924 the station tested 3.85', a planted value, loses the item.
Crate to the loft over the intake room (Story 7); notebooks to the state office 1936, college library since 1947 (Story 8).
Story 7: patrons petitioned January 1925.
The dates and two sittings in the weigh room are right, but the chair is only 'an Ashlin attorney'. Alonzo Frick is not named.
Only the theft theory is placed before the board; watering and hay are not stated as argued in 1925.
Four books including Strawn's 1923 notebook, which recorded the condemnation; 'Nobody set the receiving book beside Strawn's notebook'.
Dismissed 30 April 1925; award four days later, 'no cause established', $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account.
One-fifth of $19,000 is given, but not that the charge fell on the very account where the loss had accrued as 'gain'.
Story 8 and Story 3: b. 1931, granddaughter, State Agricultural College Farland, Leland Vaught.
Records gathered piecemeal, but no statement that they had never been in the same room; ledgers not among them.
Story 8: February 1958, station loft, nine pipettes.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 vs 17.6 (Story 8), 0.88 c.c./5% short (Story 2).
Proportional 5% low reading on glass in use 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923; 3.61 recorded vs 3.80 true, 0.19 short (Stories 2, 4, 7).
Story 6: 40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000, and the difference is the ledger's station-gain line (1,444,000 credited vs 1,520,000 received).
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; cleared 24 years after death and 33 after dismissal (list-type, core fact present).
Granddaughter; derivation through Duncan, Ansel's son.

Second cousins with correct derivation (1). The full/half question is declared unsettled, but instead of saying it does not change the answer the run says half siblings would make them 'half second cousins' (0). Abstained, so no deduction.
Gideon Vose; significance via Article 7 making the station test decide pay.
A01 asserted: 'On the evidence there was no kinship' and E row 17 'No relation.' Firsthand denial treated as settling it.
0.95, 95% of true, 5% low.
$90 at $0.25, explicitly stated as the long-run average instead of the 1910 price, with working shown. Meets the key's acceptance condition.
76,000 lb = 5.26% of fat credited and 5.00% of fat received; both denominators named.
$77.93 with line sum.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
26 years and 6 weeks vs 25 full years 1898-1922, the difference being the part years 1897 and 1923.
Abstains: 1896 intake cannot be determined; Kyle's 1.1M flagged as uncorroborated hearsay.
Variable: the measuring glass, station's own vs borrowed; 'Only the glass changed'.
Tester, herds, pasture, feed, season, machinery, acid, scales held constant.
'Rose markedly ... fell back'. No 3.80 during the interval and no 3.61 on return.
Rules out water/theft/hay; limits: which piece, size of error, borrowed measure's accuracy.
Ledger (Kyle r23), 1911 interval (Falke/Orra/Duncan), Alder Corners (Hazel r17): three valid reasons from three narrators.
Independence argued; names reasons that hold without the 1958 measurement (ledger, Alder Corners).
A09 asserted: 'no, the bookkeeper never questioned the ledger entries'.
Yes, he knew the tests ran low: 1902 complaints, 1919 circular.
Only two valid of five: signed ledger sheets, 1919 circular. The manager year is given as 1911 (wrong); no hearing argument; nothing on his never naming the glassware.

Headline 'What cannot be shown is that he understood...' / 'cannot show that he knew the cause' is read as an abstention (no -2), though it leans ('he did not register'). Fails REQUIRED: none of the observations (two office men answering oppositely, no document, no pre-1923 Vose statement, never asked) beyond at most the signature point.
Weigh book 1897 over Hazel's 1900 (she disclaims years); the 1908 committee and the 1925 board as separate bodies (Falke); Orra b. 1866 from 'eighty-two in 1948' plus the diary. Capped at 3.
NT-14 $77.39 (Junia + Chronicle, broken by the invoice total and line sum); NT-18 great-niece (Chronicle + Falke, broken by Falke's correction and the family). No third pair identified as a pair.
A04 declared undeterminable (works books burned 1931). A06 not raised. A10 abstained only in Section A, which does not carry into E.
Junia's 'nothing into Ordell before 1900' above her own 1897 invoice (also Duncan's 1868 vs 82 in 1948).
Pipettes 16.72 vs 17.6, 95%; 0.19 = 5% of 3.80; onset 1 May 1897 after borrowed glass; cessation 1923; nothing on the farms changed. The 3.85 is deducted separately.
Watering (Selby Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer and the 1911 interval.
Theft defeated by the ledger's station gain: more fat arrived than was credited.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214 (0.05 winter, nil summer vs flat 0.19) and Alder Corners.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.'
A05 asserted: tester believed 'the cause was in the glass'.
About 138 words.
Record series named explicitly: the ledger and the 1958 measurement, plus at most implied invoice, condemnation and board. Fewer than five named.
No decoy adopted and no wrong headline figure in the summary.
5% short, 1897, 76,000 lb/$19,000, 1923 condemnation, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named.

Corruption: Strawn's circuit/lactometer visits from 1908 asserted (Story 4, F2)
Corruption: 1924 station average 3.85 asserted (Story 7, D2, F1, F3)
Corruption: circular sent to eleven families asserted (Story 4; E row 12 'Eleven, provisionally')
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved as 'no kinship'/'No relation' (B4, E row 17)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper asserted never to have questioned the entries (D2)
Gullibility A07: board asserted not to have examined the glassware (F)
Gullibility A05: tester asserted to have believed the cause was in the glass (F)
